rv.q: It runs out of steam at the end, with a slightly woo-woo finale that feels needlessly silly, bordering on actual cringe.
A hugely relatable and perceptive show with generous doses of physicality.
Lost Atoms shows that the company have as much to offer the theatre 30 years on as they did as a fledgling student group.
Sad to say, it’s not so much atoms that are lost as an entire evening.

cn.t: Frantic Assembly's 30th anniversary production divides critics, with some praising its physical theatre innovation and relationship dynamics, while others find it fails to cohere despite strong performances and skilled writing.
